prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1453; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is not named on the policy and does not live with the policyholder.
text:
Entry 1: The claim was reported by the claimant's representing attorney's office after a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. The insured vehicle was struck from behind while stopped, and the claimant reported neck and back discomfort at the scene.

Entry 2: The driver of the insured vehicle is not named on the policy and does not live with the policyholder, so driver status is being reviewed against the policy terms. A recorded statement has been requested through counsel.

Entry 3: Photos submitted by the claimant show the rear bumper area and the front of the claimant's vehicle. The images confirm some of the reported impact details, but there are no independent witnesses to the collision.

Entry 4: It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting at the time of impact, and the seating position will need to be confirmed before injury causation is assessed. The claimant has described the seating position consistently so far.

Entry 5: The claimant told the same account of the collision in every conversation with this office, including the initial report and the follow-up call with counsel present. No inconsistencies have been noted in the timeline of events.

Entry 6: No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims history, and nothing suggests the damage occurred before the policy coverage started. Prior ownership records are being requested to confirm this.

Entry 7: It is not clear whether all of the damage to the claimant's vehicle came from this impact, so an independent estimate has been ordered to separate any pre-existing wear from new damage.

Entry 8: Medical records show a diagnosis of back strain. No earlier injury to the same body area is known from the records received so far, but prior provider history has been requested.

Entry 9: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this injury, and the treating provider's notes have been requested to review the treatment plan and its link to the collision.

Entry 10: It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash or from another cause. The medical reviewer has been asked to give an opinion on causation once the full records are in.

Entry 11: Next steps are to obtain the outstanding records, complete the damage estimate review, and schedule a follow-up with counsel. The file will remain open pending these items.
